_meta.description: Command card library for the Legion app. A command hand is built from exactly 7 cards: 2x 1-pip, 2x 2-pip, 2x 3-pip, and the 4-pip 'Standing Orders' -- no duplicates allowed. Generic cards (this seed) can be played by any commander in any army; commander-specific cards are owned by a named commander unit (see data/units.json) and only usable if that unit is in the army.
_meta.command_hand_rule: 2x one-pip + 2x two-pip + 2x three-pip + 1x Standing Orders (four-pip) = 7 cards total, no duplicate card names.
_meta.priority_rule: Whoever plays the command card with the fewest pips wins priority for the round and acts first in the Activation Phase; ties are broken by a defense die roll (see keywords.json/rules notes on 'Command Phase').
_meta.verification_status: SEED ONLY. Populated: the 4 faction-neutral generic command cards (Ambush/Push/Assault/Standing Orders) with pips and units-activated counts confirmed via multiple convergent sources. Effect text is paraphrased and mostly NOT verified against current exact wording (post-2024-refresh reprints may have changed details) -- see effect_verified per card. NOT populated: commander-specific command cards. Every commander unit in units.json (35 of them) typically owns ~2-3 personal command cards of their own -- that's roughly 70-100+ additional cards not yet catalogued here, plus faction-restricted and battle-force-restricted generic-ish cards (e.g. '501st Legion only') seen during research but not enumerated. See docs/TODO.md.

command_cards.name: Ambush
command_cards.effect_description: Issue an order to 1 unit. No additional special effect beyond a fast, narrow order -- lowest pip count of the four generics, so it's the most likely to win priority, at the cost of only ordering a single unit.
command_cards.roster_source: Multiple convergent sources (FFG 2018 article, wiki card pages, community rules summaries), confirmed 2026-08-22
command_cards.source: Legion Core Set (all four generics ship in the Core Set and remain in the current card pool per 2025 Updated Battle Cards reprints)

command_cards.name: Standing Orders
command_cards.effect_description: Issue an order to 1 unit. Unlike every other command card, Standing Orders returns to your hand at the end of the Command Phase instead of being spent/discarded, so it can be replayed round after round -- trades speed (highest pip count, so you're unlikely to win priority) for reusability.

command_cards.notes: The 'returns to your hand' mechanic is directly and consistently confirmed across sources; this is the one effect description in this generic seed with higher confidence.
